support.label: High-priority support ticket
support.detail: Customer Support · users may be affected

synthetics.label: Synthetic test failed
synthetics.detail: Key user journey · failed in three regions

release.label: Release health check failed
release.detail: Deployment monitor · canary check in production

discover-time-window.headline: ${param.incident.headline}
discover-time-window.summary: Some ${param.incident.journey} attempts were slow or failed, but the report didn't say exactly when it started or stopped.
discover-time-window.impact: The problem may have been short. You can see normal traffic both before and after it, so the first job is to work out exactly when it happened.

signals.label: Customer signal
signals.value: Short-lived ${param.incident.journey} failures reported

signals.label: Telemetry
signals.value: Normal and failing events are mixed in the current view

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find when the problem started and stopped

http-error-regression.headline: More server errors since the latest release
http-error-regression.summary: HTTP 5xx errors went up soon after a new release reached production. The service's overall health is red, but we don't know yet which requests are failing.
http-error-regression.impact: Some customer API calls are failing. Releases are paused until the on-call engineer finds the failing endpoint and a typical error.

signals.label: Rule
signals.value: More than 5% of responses were 5xx errors in 3 checks in a row

signals.label: Change context
signals.value: A production rollout finished recently

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the failing endpoint and the error it returns

auth-rejection-surge.headline: Many more sign-ins are being rejected than usual
auth-rejection-surge.summary: Sign-in failures are much higher than normal. Everyday rejections are mixed in with the unusual ones, which hides the real cause.
auth-rejection-surge.impact: Some customers cannot sign in. People who are already signed in are fine, so only new sign-ins are affected.

signals.label: Anomaly
signals.value: Rejections are more than 3× the usual rate

signals.label: Noise
signals.value: The total also includes normal rejections

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the unusual rejection reason

timed_facts.text: The rollout of the new release began at {time} ({ago}).

deployment-version-regression.headline: Some instances started failing during a rollout
deployment-version-regression.summary: Errors went up on only some of the service's instances during a rolling deployment. The overall health numbers hide which group of instances is different.
deployment-version-regression.impact: Some requests fail and others succeed, depending on which instance handles them. The rollout is paused until the evidence shows whether the new version is the cause.

signals.label: Fleet health
signals.value: Instances that should be the same give different results

signals.label: Change context
signals.value: The rolling deployment happened during the incident

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Compare results for each service version

rare-error-signature.headline: A rare exception may be causing failed requests
rare-error-signature.summary: A busy service is mostly healthy, but one rare exception seems to be linked to failed customer requests.
rare-error-signature.impact: The error rate is still low, so the problem is easy to miss on dashboards. The team that owns the service needs two things: the exception's name and one failed request that shows it.

signals.label: Error budget
signals.value: The error budget is being used up fast, even though most requests succeed

signals.label: Cardinality
signals.value: Many routine messages, and only a few important exceptions

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the rare exception and one request where it happened

schema-drift-data-quality.headline: A dashboard's request count dropped suddenly
schema-drift-data-quality.summary: The dashboard only counts requests that have a value in the http.route field. That count fell, but the total number of incoming requests stayed the same.
schema-drift-data-quality.impact: Reports that use this data may be missing requests. Before teams trust the dashboard again, they need to know which telemetry producer stopped filling in http.route.

signals.label: Dashboard
signals.value: Far fewer requests with http.route than usual

signals.label: Ingress
signals.value: The total number of requests is normal

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the producer and version that stopped sending http.route

log-pattern-noise-reduction.headline: Warning logs jumped while requests were failing
log-pattern-noise-reduction.summary: The service logs are full of thousands of repeated warnings. Most of them are not a problem, and only one pattern seems to be linked to failed requests.
log-pattern-noise-reduction.impact: The number of warnings alone does not show what is wrong. The pattern that matters must be separated from the background noise before anyone can fix the problem.

signals.label: Log volume
signals.value: More than 10× the usual number of warnings

signals.label: Customer signal
signals.value: Failed requests went up at the same time

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the log pattern linked to the failures

esql-top-failing-routes.headline: The public API is failing on several routes
esql-top-failing-routes.summary: More requests are failing than usual. Counting errors alone can make busy routes look worst, and hide a smaller route that fails more often.
esql-top-failing-routes.impact: Several customer journeys may be affected. The incident lead needs the routes ranked by failure count and failure rate before deciding who works on what.

signals.label: SLO
signals.value: The API is using up its error budget fast enough to page someone

signals.label: Scope
signals.value: Several routes are adding to the alert

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Rank the routes by failures and failure rate

esql-before-after-deploy.headline: Service health changed after a release
esql-before-after-deploy.summary: Latency and errors seem higher since a recent release. Normal changes in traffic make the trend on the chart hard to judge.
esql-before-after-deploy.impact: The rollout is paused halfway. Release Engineering needs before-and-after numbers to decide whether to roll back or continue.

signals.label: Guardrail
signals.value: Latency and error checks are outside their normal limits

signals.label: Decision
signals.value: No rollback until the numbers are in

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Compare the periods before and after the deployment

esql-cross-service-summary.headline: A checkout incident affects several services
esql-cross-service-summary.summary: The incident touches several services. Each has its own dashboard, so request volume, failures and tail latency are hard to compare.
esql-cross-service-summary.impact: It isn't clear which team should respond. The incident lead needs one table of each service's health to decide where engineers should look first.

signals.label: Topology
signals.value: Several services appear in the affected requests

signals.label: Tail latency
signals.value: The slowest requests take much longer than normal

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Show volume, failures and p95 for each service

dashboard-incident-triage.headline: A regional health alarm needs quick triage
dashboard-incident-triage.summary: The service overview shows one unusual problem in production. The alert doesn't say which region, service or time period is affected.
dashboard-incident-triage.impact: Customer requests are failing or slow in at least one region. The incident lead needs to know the scope quickly, before paging more teams.

signals.label: Overview
signals.value: One unusual problem in the current dashboard time range

signals.label: Scope
signals.value: Region and service not confirmed yet

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find where and when the impact happened

dashboard-drilldown-to-evidence.headline: A dashboard spike needs checking in the documents behind it
dashboard-drilldown-to-evidence.summary: The service overview shows a sharp spike in failures. Keep its time range and filters while you move from the chart to the raw events.
dashboard-drilldown-to-evidence.impact: The chart looks real, but nobody can act on it yet. One source document is needed before an engineering team can own the issue.

signals.label: Dashboard
signals.value: A short, sharp spike in failures

signals.label: Evidence gap
signals.value: No example source document attached yet

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Drill down without losing the time range and filters

dashboard-panel-inspection.headline: Two dashboard panels disagree
dashboard-panel-inspection.summary: Two panels about service health seem to disagree. Check how each one is calculated and filtered before using either for an incident decision.
dashboard-panel-inspection.impact: People are getting status updates that don't agree. The on-call engineer must show which panel answers the question, and why.

signals.label: Dashboard
signals.value: Panels side by side show different health states

signals.label: Risk
signals.value: The metrics may be based on different data

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Inspect how each panel is calculated and filtered

slow-dependency-trace.headline: Checkout p95 latency is over the customer SLO
slow-dependency-trace.summary: Checkout requests are completing slowly in production. The first service still responds, so the time is probably spent deeper in its dependencies.
slow-dependency-trace.impact: Customers wait several seconds to confirm an order, and some give up. The on-call engineer needs the downstream operation that takes up the trace's critical path.

signals.label: SLO
signals.value: Checkout p95 above 2.5 s for 3 windows

signals.label: Probe
signals.value: The order confirmation step is always slow

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the slow dependency and operation

trace-error-propagation.headline: The edge service returns upstream errors without details
trace-error-propagation.summary: The public edge reports a general error, but its own logs don't contain the exception that caused it. Follow the failure through the distributed trace.
trace-error-propagation.impact: Customers see failed requests with no useful explanation. No team can own the issue until we know which span failed first and how the error spread.

signals.label: Edge response
signals.value: A general upstream error is returned to clients

signals.label: Trace state
signals.value: The error status spreads across service boundaries

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the first exception in the trace

retry-amplification.headline: Dependency traffic rose without more users
retry-amplification.summary: Calls to a downstream dependency got more frequent and slower, while customer traffic stayed fairly steady. Retries may be multiplying the calls.
retry-amplification.impact: The dependency may get several calls for each user request. That adds load and makes the critical path longer. The team needs proof from traces before changing the retry policy.

signals.label: Traffic ratio
signals.value: Dependency calls are growing faster than incoming requests

signals.label: Latency
signals.value: Time spent on repeated downstream calls is adding up

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Compare traces and prove the calls repeat

trace-log-correlation.headline: A payment trace failed without the exception details
trace-log-correlation.summary: A customer payment trace ends in failure, but its span metadata doesn't include the application error needed to explain it.
trace-log-correlation.impact: The payment could not complete, and first-line support has no useful error reason. Use the trace and its time to find the exact application log.

signals.label: Trace
signals.value: The failed payment request is captured from start to end

signals.label: Evidence gap
signals.value: The span metadata has no exception details

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the application log linked to the trace

cpu-saturation.headline: Service latency went up during a traffic peak
cpu-saturation.summary: One production service got slower as traffic rose. High CPU use is suspected, but nobody has checked that it happened at the same time as the slowdown.
cpu-saturation.impact: Customers see slower responses under load. Capacity changes should wait until someone proves that CPU pressure matches the incident in time.

signals.label: APM
signals.value: Service response time is above its normal range

signals.label: Load
signals.value: The traffic peak overlaps the suspected time

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Compare service latency with CPU use over time

memory-leak-and-restarts.headline: A workload is restarting more and more often
memory-leak-and-restarts.summary: A long-running workload has become unstable over several hours. The restarts may come from memory growing steadily, not from one traffic spike.
memory-leak-and-restarts.impact: Requests can fail or be retried while instances restart. The platform team needs the resource trend and the first restart before changing limits or rolling back.

signals.label: Workload
signals.value: Restarts are above their normal baseline

signals.label: Time horizon
signals.value: The problem built up over several hours

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Connect the memory trend to the first restart

hot-instance-imbalance.headline: Fleet averages hide one overloaded instance
hot-instance-imbalance.summary: Overall service health looks fine, but one instance uses far more resources than the others. It also responds more slowly.
hot-instance-imbalance.impact: Only requests sent to that instance are slow, so the problem comes and goes. Find the instance, and compare it with healthy ones before replacing it.

signals.label: Fleet average
signals.value: Within normal limits, although latency comes and goes

signals.label: Distribution
signals.value: Resource use seems uneven between instances

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the outlier and check that the other instances are healthy

capacity-throughput-saturation.headline: Latency rises sharply above a certain throughput
capacity-throughput-saturation.summary: The service is healthy at normal load but slows down when traffic is high. Use the evidence to find where it starts to saturate, not one peak reading.
capacity-throughput-saturation.impact: Peak demand is pushing customer latency past the SLO. Capacity Engineering needs the rough throughput where latency starts to climb, to plan safe scaling and admission-control changes.

signals.label: SLO
signals.value: Tail latency goes over the SLO only under high load

signals.label: Pattern
signals.value: The data has both healthy and saturated periods

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Estimate the throughput saturation point

active-alert-triage.headline: A fulfilment customer-failure alert is firing
active-alert-triage.summary: A new alert fired for a fulfilment service you don't know well. Its reason suggests customers are affected, but check it against the current source events.
active-alert-triage.impact: Shipment requests may be failing. Treat it as urgent only if the condition still holds and production events back up the alert's reason.

signals.label: Rule
signals.value: Fulfilment customer failures

signals.label: Evaluation
signals.value: The alert condition was met in the latest check

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Set the priority and point to the source events

slow-payments.headline: Checkout is slower than the latency SLO allows
slow-payments.summary: Customers report that checkout has become slow in the last few minutes. The delay is visible at the edge, but the service causing it has not been found.
slow-payments.impact: Some customers wait more than three seconds to place an order, and may give up. The on-call engineer needs evidence from the requests involved before paging a downstream owner.

signals.label: SLO
signals.value: Checkout p95 above 3 s for 3 windows

signals.label: Route
signals.value: POST /checkout · production

signals.label: Triage request
signals.value: Find the bottleneck with trace evidence
